relevant_findings.topic: Fiber cement substrate composition and coating behavior
relevant_findings.finding: Fiber cement (James Hardie, Allura, Nichiha) is a cementitious composite of portland cement, silica, and cellulose fibers. Dense (~2.3 lbs/SF), non-combustible, dimensionally stable. The face surface is non-porous but the cementitious matrix can reach pH 13.0 — critical for primer compatibility on bare/damaged surfaces. Cut edges are porous and absorb moisture via cellulose capillaries.

relevant_findings.topic: Factory prime is transit protection only
relevant_findings.finding: All fiber cement siding ships with factory primer applied. This is transit and weather protection — NOT finish-ready. Field prime coat is REQUIRED before topcoat application for both adhesion performance and manufacturer warranty compliance. Factory-primed products must be top-coated within 180 days or primer degradation occurs.

The most critical failure mode for fiber cement. Liquid water absorbs into unsealed cut ends via cellulose fiber capillary action, causing edge swelling that ruptures paint film. ALL field-cut edges must be sealed with end-cut sealer or field primer before installation. This is non-negotiable for warranty and performance.

relevant_findings.topic: Back-rolling is AVOIDED on fiber cement
relevant_findings.finding: Per Application Methods Doctrine, back-rolling fiber cement introduces unwanted stipple/orange peel texture on the factory-smooth surface. Spray-only application is correct for fiber cement lap siding and panels. This is a key difference from wood siding where back-rolling may be mandatory on weathered/rough surfaces.

relevant_findings.topic: Alkaline primer requirement for bare fiber cement
relevant_findings.finding: Bare/exposed fiber cement (pH 13.0) requires alkali-resistant primer (e.g., SW Loxon Masonry Primer or equivalent alkali-resistant acrylic) to prevent saponification ('alkaline burn') of latex binders. Standard acrylic exterior primer is NOT suitable for bare fiber cement. Unprimed fiber cement must be painted within 90 days of exposure.

relevant_findings.topic: Surface texture factor for production and material
relevant_findings.finding: Deeply embossed textures (Cedarmill, roughsawn grain profiles) require a surface_factor of 1.15-1.30 vs. smooth board for both material consumption (achieves correct DFT on textured profile) and production rate (additional spray passes needed). Smooth HardiePlank has no surface factor penalty.

Three fiber cement siding profiles in scope: HardiePlank lap siding (horizontal), HardieShingle (individual or panel shingles), HardiePanel (vertical flat panels). Each profile has distinct production rate characteristics. Lap siding is fastest (long horizontal runs), shingle is slowest (many edges, complex geometry).

James Hardie warranty requires use of specific approved paint systems (SW Duration, SW Emerald, or other Hardie-approved products) with 2 coats required per warranty. Field prime over factory prime is mandatory for warranty validity.

High-pressure power washing is PROHIBITED on fiber cement — strips paint films, damages surface texture, forces water behind wall assembly. Acid washing is also prohibited. Use low-pressure water spray (garden hose) with soft to medium bristle brush for cleaning.

relevant_findings.topic: ColorPlus / factory-finished fiber cement is IN SCOPE
relevant_findings.finding: James Hardie ColorPlus Technology and similar factory-finished fiber cement products (multi-coat oven-baked factory finish) are IN SCOPE for this spec. It is common for factory-finished siding to require full primer and paint after construction — caulking, installation damage, handling marks, and construction activity compromise the factory finish to the point where field painting is required. Treat factory-finished fiber cement as a substrate state that requires bonding primer before topcoat, since the oven-baked factory finish is a non-standard substrate for field paint adhesion.

condition_drivers.impact: Drives primer selection (field prime on factory-primed; alkali-resistant primer on bare; bonding primer on factory-finished), prep sequence, and coat count.
condition_drivers.notes: SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY is the dominant NC state. SS_EXT_BARE_FIBERCEMENT occurs at damaged areas or cut edges. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD means field prime already applied. SS_EXT_FACTORY_FINISHED covers ColorPlus/ExpertFinish products damaged during construction — requires bonding primer.

condition_drivers.impact: Production rate varies dramatically. Lap: fastest (long horizontal runs). Panel: moderate (large flat areas). Shingle: slowest (many edges, complex geometry). Profile also affects spray tip selection and coverage rate.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a configuration dimension, not a site condition.

condition_drivers.impact: Textured profiles require 15-30% more material (surface_factor 1.15-1.30) and slightly slower spray production. Smooth profiles spray at baseline rate.
condition_drivers.notes: Surface_factor modifier on material quantity and production rate.

condition_drivers.impact: QT2: economy application, single coat acceptable on primed surfaces. QT3: standard 2-coat with clean cut-in. QT4: premium materials (SW Emerald, BM Aura), light sand between coats, raking light inspection. QT5 is not applicable to siding field — reserved for fine exterior millwork only.
condition_drivers.notes: Per Exterior_Substrates_Doctrine.md §5. QT5 excluded for siding field.

condition_drivers.impact: Spray is primary method for fiber cement (factory-smooth surface, no back-rolling). Brush_roll is fallback for small projects <750 SF, occupied adjacent areas, or high wind conditions. Back-rolling is explicitly AVOIDED on fiber cement.
condition_drivers.notes: Per Application Methods Doctrine Part A §6 — back-rolling introduces unwanted texture on smooth fiber cement.

condition_drivers.impact: Height modifier on all tasks at elevation. ground=1.00, ladder=1.35, scaffold=1.60, lift=1.50. Applied per elevation based on working height.
condition_drivers.notes: Treated as a HEIGHT MODIFIER (like FAC_HEIGHT for interior), not a site condition. A project may have ground access on one elevation and scaffold on another.

quality_differences.description: Economy exterior. Light clean, spot repair only. Single finish coat acceptable on factory-primed/field-primed surfaces. Economy-grade 100% acrylic exterior. No edge precision required.
Standard residential. Full low-pressure wash. Field prime over factory prime (mandatory). Two finish coats with mid-grade 100% acrylic. Clean cut-in at trim lines. Caulk all siding-to-trim joints.
quality_differences.typical_use: Standard homeowner NC, most residential exterior fiber cement.

quality_differences.description: Premium exterior. Full wash with TSP. Field prime with premium primer. Two finish coats with premium materials (SW Emerald, BM Aura — Hardie-approved). Light sand between coats on visible areas. Raking light inspection before second coat. Crisp trim lines.
quality_differences.typical_use: High-end residential, showcase homes, curb-appeal priority.

failure_modes.name: Edge wicking / capillary rise
failure_modes.description: Unsealed cut edges absorb liquid water via cellulose fiber capillaries. Edge swelling ruptures paint film from behind. Most common field failure on fiber cement.
failure_modes.prevention: Seal ALL field-cut edges with end-cut sealer or field primer before installation or as early as possible after cutting.
failure_modes.detection: Swollen board edges, paint bubbling at cut ends, visible moisture staining at board joints.

failure_modes.name: Alkaline burn / saponification
failure_modes.description: Unneutralized bare fiber cement (pH 13.0) chemically destroys latex binders, causing paint film to soften, blister, and detach.
failure_modes.prevention: Use alkali-resistant primer (2-component epoxy or specialized acrylic sealer) on all bare fiber cement surfaces. Never apply standard latex directly to bare fiber cement.
failure_modes.detection: Soft, sticky paint film. Paint easily scrapes off with fingernail. Yellow-brown discoloration.

failure_modes.name: Efflorescence
failure_modes.description: Water evaporating from fiber cement board leaves soluble white salt deposits that physically push paint film off the wall.
failure_modes.prevention: Ensure proper wall assembly drainage (WRB, flashing). Field prime to seal surface before topcoat. Address moisture source.
failure_modes.detection: White crystalline deposits on or under paint film. Paint blistering or peeling with white powder underneath.

failure_modes.name: Joint cracking from thermal/hygroscopic movement
failure_modes.description: Tight-butted siding installed without expansion gaps leads to thermal and hygroscopic movement that buckles boards or cracks inflexible caulking at joints.
failure_modes.prevention: Ensure proper installation gaps per manufacturer specs. Use flexible paintable caulk at siding-to-trim joints. Recommend joint flashing (slipsheets) behind field butt joints rather than relying on caulk.
failure_modes.detection: Cracked caulk at joints. Board buckle or bow. Gaps opening and closing seasonally.

failure_modes.name: Factory primer degradation from exposure
failure_modes.description: Factory primer on fiber cement degrades if exposed beyond 180 days. Primer becomes chalky, loses adhesion, and no longer provides suitable base for field prime or topcoat.
failure_modes.prevention: Field-prime and paint within 180 days of installation. If exposure exceeds 180 days, assess factory primer adhesion. May require sanding and re-priming.
failure_modes.detection: Chalky primer surface. Poor adhesion when tested with tape pull or knife edge.

notes_for_materials_manager: Fiber cement requires Hardie-approved topcoat systems (SW Duration, SW Emerald, BM Aura or equivalent) for warranty compliance.

Field primer: 100% acrylic exterior primer for factory-primed surfaces (standard). Alkali-resistant primer (e.g., SW Loxon Masonry Primer) for bare fiber cement to maintain proper pH and prevent alkaline burn. Bonding primer for factory-finished (ColorPlus/ExpertFinish) surfaces.
Coverage rate for fiber cement: 300-350 SF/gal per coat on smooth; apply surface_factor 1.15-1.30 for textured (Cedarmill/roughsawn).
Transfer efficiency: spray application has 50-70% transfer (25-33% more material than brush/roll). Factor into material quantities.
Spray tip: 515 or 517 for lap siding, 413 for shingle profiles. 60-mesh (black) filter for latex.
End-cut sealer is a separate consumable — needed for all field-cut edges.
Caulk: flexible paintable caulk (polyurethane or siliconized acrylic) for siding-to-trim joints.

ColorPlus and ExpertFinish factory-finished products are IN SCOPE as SS_EXT_FACTORY_FINISHED — requires bonding primer (oven-baked factory finish is non-standard substrate for field paint adhesion) before standard topcoat system.
notes_for_sop_librarian: Edge seal task is MANDATORY for SS_EXT_BARE_FIBERCEMENT and SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY (cut edges during installation). Include as conditional task in prep module.
Field prime is MANDATORY over factory prime (SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY). Not optional. Include as required task in prime module.
NO back-rolling on fiber cement. Spray-only finish application. This is a departure from wood siding spec.
Power washing PROHIBITED on fiber cement. Low-pressure wash only (garden hose + soft brush).
Module structure: setup → protect → clean → prep → prime → apply → cleanup → teardown.
Shingle profile requires significantly different task sequencing — more edge work, constant repositioning, lower production.
SS_EXT_BARE_FIBERCEMENT triggers alkali-resistant primer path (e.g., SW Loxon Masonry Primer — separate from standard field prime).
SS_EXT_FACTORY_FINISHED triggers bonding primer path — oven-baked factory finish requires bonding primer for field paint adhesion. Light scuff sand entire surface before prime.
Caulking at siding-to-trim joints is a prep module task. Do NOT caulk field butt joints on lap siding (moisture trap).
Light sand between coats at QT4 only (not QT2 or QT3).
notes_for_estimation_engineer: Production rates vary significantly by profile: lap spray ~250-400 SF/hr, panel spray ~200-350 SF/hr, shingle spray ~100-150 SF/hr.
Brush/roll rates: lap ~80-120 SF/hr, panel ~60-100 SF/hr, shingle ~30-50 SF/hr.
Access modifier (FAC_EXT_ACCESS): ground=1.00, ladder=1.35, scaffold=1.60, lift=1.50.
Surface texture modifier: smooth=1.00, cedarmill/roughsawn=1.15-1.30 on BOTH material and production.
End seal task rate: ~60-80 EA/hr (brush sealant on cut ends).
Field prime rate: ~300-450 SF/hr spray on factory-primed fiber cement.
Environmental conditions (wind, dew point, sun, temp) are EXCLUDED from estimation — they are SOP/process concerns, not estimatable at bid time.
Masking-to-spray ratio: 3:1 to 4:1 (masking hours to spray hours). Masking is a separate line item.
Coat system: 1 field prime + 2 finish coats standard at all QTs for NC. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD skips prime.
QT2 may use single finish coat on field-primed surfaces — per Exterior_Substrates_Doctrine §4.5.

assumptions.value: New construction fiber cement siding field painting only (not trim, not soffit, not factory-finished products)
assumptions.note: Trim around fiber cement siding is covered by separate exterior trim spec. Soffit covered by separate soffit spec.

assumptions.value: Avoid — spray only on fiber cement face
assumptions.note: Explicit doctrine guidance: 'Fiber cement (Hardiplank): Back-rolling introduces unwanted stipple/orange peel — spray-only for factory-smooth finish.'

assumptions.value: QT5 not applicable to siding field applications
assumptions.note: QT5 reserved for fine exterior millwork, columns, decorative elements. Not siding field.

uncertainties.detail: Doctrine references James Hardie and Allura by name. Nichiha fiber cement may have different primer/topcoat warranty requirements. Nichiha products should be validated against manufacturer PDS before spec finalization.
uncertainties.recommendation: Add Nichiha as a manufacturer variant in materials.json with a note to verify PDS.

uncertainties.detail: Shingle profile production rates (100-150 SF/hr spray, 30-50 SF/hr brush) are extrapolated from wood shingle rates in the wood siding spec. Fiber cement shingles may be slightly faster due to more uniform geometry, but no direct doctrine calibration exists.
uncertainties.recommendation: Flag shingle profile rates for field calibration. Use wood shingle rates as conservative baseline.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray
zones.notes: LF-based — measured along house perimeter where landscape is adjacent. Brush/roll: drop cloth at base. Spray: full tarp width over plantings. You measure the run along the house, not the area of landscape beds.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray
zones.notes: Adjacent walkways. Brush/roll: drop cloth runners. Spray: full tarp coverage.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray
zones.notes: Adjacent patio surfaces. Protection level driven by proximity and application method.
Exterior light fixtures mounted on or adjacent to siding. Bag or tape over fixture.
HVAC condenser units adjacent to siding. Full tarp cover during spray operations.

protection_zones_analysis.cross_spec_protection_note: Window and door protection during siding work is NOT this spec's responsibility. Window/door masking (glass, hardware, full unit cover) belongs in the respective window or door spec. If windows/doors are not being painted, their protection is scoped under the window/door spec or a separate protection mobilization. This prevents double-counting and ensures protection responsibility is clear per surface owner.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Soffit underside at eave. Often different color (white/light). Siding terminates at soffit/frieze junction. Separate scope.
Frieze board — horizontal trim board at the junction between siding and soffit/eave. Often a different (trim) color. Separate trim scope.
Corner boards frame siding field. Often different color (accent trim). Siding field terminates at corner board. Separate trim scope.
Window casing trim around openings. Siding terminates at casing. No cut-in — trim is a separate spec.
Door casing trim. Same as window casing relationship. Separate spec.
Foundation below siding. Not painted in siding scope. Drop cloth protection at grade level.

adjacency_analysis.key_finding: Identical adjacency pattern to wood siding — siding field has NO edge work requirements. All adjacent surfaces are separate specs (soffit, trim, foundation) or not in scope. Protection relationships only. Siding terminates at trim boards. Window/door protection owned by window/door specs.

affected_conditions.notes: Access type drives a HEIGHT MODIFIER on tasks, NOT a site condition. Applied per elevation based on working height. A project may have ground access on one elevation and scaffold on another.

excluded_conditions.rationale: Environmental conditions (wind, dew point, sun exposure, surface temperature) are important to the painting PROCESS but are NOT estimatable. They are unpredictable, change daily, and cannot be set as fixed conditions for an estimate. Including them adds estimation complexity with no practical benefit. They belong in SOP procedure notes and job-site decision protocols, not in production rate modifiers.

excluded.reason: Unpredictable. Changes hourly. Cannot set a fixed modifier for estimate.
Varies by time of day, sun angle, and season. Not predictable at bid time.
Weather-dependent. Not predictable at bid time.
Varies by elevation and season. Professional painters follow the shade — scheduling, not estimation.

valid_input_states.rationale: NC fiber cement siding arrives factory-primed (dominant state). Bare fiber cement occurs at cut edges or damaged areas. Field-primed means primer already applied — ready for topcoat. Factory-finished (ColorPlus/equivalent) is included because post-construction damage and caulking commonly compromise the factory finish, requiring field prime + paint.

output_state.rationale: Output state is the painted finish. Satin is the most common exterior siding sheen. Actual output varies by sheen configuration (flat, satin, semi-gloss).

adjacent_state_protection_analysis.rationale: Protect finished trim from siding spray overspray. Unfinished trim needs no protection — it will be painted later.

Soffit is typically painted before siding (top-down sequencing). If already finished, light masking at the siding-soffit junction. Spray overspray drift is primarily downward/lateral — soffit is overhead and receives less direct exposure.
Foundation wall is rarely painted in NC context. Drop cloth at grade level is handled by landscape/hardscape protection zones, not adjacent surface protection.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Factory-primed fiber cement siding as delivered. Factory primer is transit/weather protection — NOT finish-ready.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Low-pressure wash (garden hose, NO pressure washer). Light sand for adhesion profile. Spot-prime any damaged/bare areas.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: Field prime: 100% acrylic exterior primer over factory prime
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Primary NC state. Field prime is MANDATORY for warranty compliance and adhesion performance. Must be top-coated within 180 days of installation or factory primer degrades.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Raw fiber cement with factory primer absent or damaged. Cut edges exposed. pH 13.0 cementitious surface.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Seal cut edges with end-cut sealer. Clean. Light sand.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: Alkali-resistant primer (2-component epoxy or specialized acrylic sealer) — standard acrylic NOT suitable for bare fiber cement at pH 13
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Occurs at field-cut edges and areas where factory primer is damaged, missing, or scraped during installation. Alkaline burn prevention is critical. Unprimed exposure must not exceed 90 days.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Fiber cement with field-applied exterior primer — ready for topcoat.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Light dust-off. Minimal prep — surface is paint-ready.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Assumes proper exterior primer was applied. Direct topcoat application. This state occurs when prime and finish are split across mobilizations.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Factory-finished fiber cement (ColorPlus Technology or equivalent). Multi-coat oven-baked finish that has been compromised by construction activity, caulking, handling damage, or general construction wear.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Low-pressure wash. Light scuff sand entire surface for adhesion profile. Clean caulk residue and construction debris.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: Bonding primer — the oven-baked factory finish is a non-standard substrate for field paint adhesion. Bonding primer ensures mechanical grip on the cured factory topcoat.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Common NC scenario. Factory-finished siding arrives looking good but after installation, caulking, and construction traffic the finish is no longer acceptable. Field prime with bonding primer + 2 topcoats restores appearance. The factory finish warranty is effectively void once field painting is performed.

exterior_access_type_analysis.treatment: Modifier on tasks, not a site condition. Same concept as FAC_HEIGHT for interior.

scenarios.notes: Single-story siding, first 8 ft. No ladder needed. Baseline rate.
Two-story siding, gable ends, areas above 8 ft. Constant repositioning. Safety overhead.
Large continuous areas above 8 ft. Setup/teardown amortized. Better than ladder for runs >50 LF.
Boom/scissor lift for 3+ story or difficult access. Requires firm ground. Rental cost.

exterior_environmental_constraints.note: Environmental constraints are documented here for SOP reference but are EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers per RC-003 correction from wood siding spec.

sop_reference_only.note: Below 50°F: slow cure, adhesion risk. Above 85°F: flash dry, blistering on dark colors.

sop_reference_only.rule: Surface temp must be ≥ 5°F above dew point
sop_reference_only.note: Adhesion and blushing risk at marginal conditions.

sop_reference_only.rule: Fiber cement: not saturated. Wood backing: < 15% MC.
sop_reference_only.note: Siding must not be painted while saturated.

production_rate_research.source: Exterior_Application_Methods_Doctrine.md, Exterior_Engineered_Wood_Fiber_Cement_Doctrine.md, calibrated against sibling spec SF_WOOD_SIDING_EXT_NC_PAINT_v1

lap_spray.notes: Airless spray, smooth or textured lap siding. 517 tip. Higher end for long uninterrupted runs.

lap_brush_roll.notes: Brush for edges/transitions, roller for field. Fallback method.

shingle_spray.notes: Complex profile, many edges. 413 tip. Constant repositioning.

shingle_brush_roll.notes: Extremely labor-intensive. Each shingle edge requires brush attention.

panel_spray.notes: Large flat panels. Similar to lap but fewer joints. 517 tip.

panel_brush_roll.notes: Roller for field, brush at panel joints and edges.

field_prime_spray.notes: Spray primer on factory-primed surface. Straightforward — good adhesion base.

low_pressure_wash.notes: Garden hose + soft brush. Faster than pressure wash because lower setup.

caulk_siding_joints.notes: Siding-to-trim joint caulking. Gun + finger tool.

key_decisions.decision: Combined (full phase_scope). Prime and finish phases have unique task keys within the single spec.
key_decisions.rationale: NC fiber cement siding is a single-mobilization scope — same crew primes and paints. Each phase (prime, finish) has its own task IDs and module IDs for independent rate tracking and phase-level reporting. Matches wood siding sibling spec pattern.

key_decisions.decision: Include siding_profile dimension: lap, shingle, panel
key_decisions.rationale: Production rates vary dramatically by profile (lap spray 300+ SF/hr vs shingle spray 100 SF/hr). Profile affects spray tip selection and coverage rate.

key_decisions.decision: Back-rolling is AVOIDED on fiber cement — spray-only finish application.
key_decisions.rationale: Per Exterior_Application_Methods_Doctrine Part A §6: 'Fiber cement (Hardiplank): Back-rolling introduces unwanted stipple/orange peel — spray-only for factory-smooth finish.' This is a key departure from wood siding where back-rolling may be required on weathered/rough surfaces.

key_decisions.decision: Four NC-relevant states: SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY, SS_EXT_BARE_FIBERCEMENT, SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD, SS_EXT_FACTORY_FINISHED. Repaint states excluded.
key_decisions.rationale: This is a new construction spec. Factory-finished (ColorPlus) included because post-construction damage commonly requires field painting. Repaint states (SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT, SS_EXT_CHALKING, SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT, SS_EXT_PEELING) would require a separate repaint spec with fundamentally different prep modules.

key_decisions.topic: Surface texture as modifier vs dimension
key_decisions.decision: Surface texture (smooth, cedarmill, roughsawn) is a MODIFIER on production and material, not a configuration dimension.
key_decisions.rationale: Texture affects rate and material quantity (surface_factor 1.15-1.30) but does not change the task structure or module sequence. It is a multiplier, not a workflow branch.

key_decisions.decision: NOT this spec's responsibility. Per wood siding sibling spec RC-001.
key_decisions.rationale: Window/door protection belongs in window/door specs. Prevents double-counting. Clear ownership per surface.

key_decisions.decision: EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers. Per wood siding sibling spec RC-003.
key_decisions.rationale: Environmental conditions are unpredictable at bid time. They are SOP/process concerns documented for field reference but not included in production rate modifiers.

key_decisions.decision: Treated as a HEIGHT MODIFIER, not a site condition. Per wood siding sibling spec RC-004.
key_decisions.rationale: Access type drives a rate multiplier on tasks at elevation — conceptually identical to FAC_HEIGHT for interior.

key_decisions.decision: 1 field prime + 2 finish coats standard at all tiers for NC.
key_decisions.rationale: James Hardie warranty requires 2 topcoats. Field prime over factory prime is mandatory. QT2 may accept single finish coat on field-primed surfaces per Exterior_Substrates_Doctrine §4.5.

key_decisions.decision: Factory-finished products (ColorPlus, ExpertFinish) are IN SCOPE as substrate state SS_EXT_FACTORY_FINISHED.
key_decisions.rationale: Post-construction damage, caulking, handling, and general construction activity commonly compromise the factory finish to the point where field painting is required. This is a real and common NC scenario. Requires bonding primer (factory baked finish is non-standard substrate for field paint adhesion) + standard topcoat system.

research_corrections.original_claim: ColorPlus and ExpertFinish factory-finished products are OUT OF SCOPE for this NC painting spec
research_corrections.corrected_to: Factory-finished fiber cement (ColorPlus, ExpertFinish) is IN SCOPE as substrate state SS_EXT_FACTORY_FINISHED. Post-construction damage, caulking, and handling commonly compromise the factory finish, requiring field prime (bonding primer) + paint.

research_corrections.original_claim: Alkali-resistant primer described generically as '2-component epoxy or specialized acrylic sealer'
research_corrections.corrected_to: SW Loxon Masonry Primer identified as the reference product for alkali-resistant primer on bare fiber cement to maintain proper pH and prevent alkaline burn.
